summary: THE HIGH REFUTATION REPRODUCED AND IS FIXED AS A DISTINCTION, NOT A REWORDING. On the tree as I found it, `python3 build1.py '{"CAP_TARGETS":"vocab","CAP_VOCAB_START":"1000"}'` printed `Gate cap.clamp: UNREACHABLE (...) -- no lift can be earned at all on this configuration, so no lift can be held at a ceiling either: the vocabulary arm has room to earn (1000 against a hard ceiling of 4096) and LM_MASK_DEAD_ROWS=False, so observe refuses every lift it earns by name as dead_rows_unmasked ...` -- pasted from my terminal, not relayed. On MY OWN 25,344-cell sweep (7 axes, listed below) 3,464 cells printed a cap.clamp reason containing both 'no lift can be earned at all' and a clause naming lifts that ARE earned (3,040 dead_rows_unmasked + 424 ONE EARNED LIFT DOES NOT MOVE IT). AFTER: 0 of 25,344. THE FIX IS THE DISTINCTION THE TASK ASKED FOR. cap.clamp reports ONE event -- an APPLIED lift HELD AT THE HARD CEILING -- and its unreachable arm now says only what is true of that: 'NO LIFT CAN BE HELD AT A HARD CEILING on this configuration ... A clamp needs three things IN ORDER -- a lift EARNED, that lift APPLIED rather than refused, and its unclamped arithmetic ABOVE the hard ceiling -- and on every arm here one of the three fails first: ...'. new_valve now builds a SECOND, STRUCTURED list `dead_facts` in the same branches that build cap.valve's prose -- (arm, kind, numbers) over the closed set _CLAMP_BLOCKED_KINDS = unarmed / nonpositive / never_pins / at_ceiling / refused_unmasked / inert -- and the new capacity/api.py::_clamp_blocked_clause writes the CLAMP'S OWN sentence for each. The two Gates now share a COMPUTED VALUE and no sentence; the splice `dead_reason="; ".join(dead)` is gone. The three reasons the old arm collapsed are each named by their own kind: (i) nothing earned = unarmed/never_pins/nonpositive, (ii) earned then refused = at_ceiling/refused_unmasked, (iii) earned, applied, moves nothing = inert. PROVED THE WAY THE REFUTATION WAS: 25,344 cells before and after; ZERO verdict moves on any of the three gates (cap.valve, cap.vocab_arm_honest, cap.clamp), zero resolved-cap or origin changes, zero build errors either side, and a SEPARATE verifier that re-derives the classification independently of api.py and checks each printed clause's arithmetic directly -- 21,608 UNREACHABLE cells, 43,216 clauses (two per cell, both arms always explained), 0 violations, 0 borrowed cap.valve prose. cap.vocab_arm_honest is byte-identical on all 25,344. cap.valve changed text on 330 cells and every one is the single reworded class (the unmasked-AND-inert arm that used to be called one that 'has room to earn'); prefix-identical up to the reworded clause, 0 verdict moves. The 'one lift ->' arithmetic is untouched: 30,885 segments parsed on each side, identical partition (11,974 plain / 4,146 CLAMPED / 14,765 at_hard_ceiling refusals), 0 plain values above a ceiling, 0 lowerings, every CLAMPED rendering has raw > ceiling == printed and every refusal has A == cap, B == ceiling, A >= B. I ALSO FIXED, IN MY OWN FILES: the two DEFERRED findings' substance (the observe/D16 present-tense overclaim in _clamped_lift's docstring, and levers.py's 'five' K13 count, re-measured to SEVEN with K13's own scanner and re-measured AGAIN after my edit because my first replacement text pushed it to NINE by respelling the patterns); api.py:37 'both its Gates' -> 'all THREE'; the three split citations (api.py's spine/derive.py::lift_to, levers.py's spine/derive.py::operating_population and src/eval/levers.py::EVALLevers) reflowed onto one line, which took O13's opened count from 684 to 693; and the CAP.counters stale-arithmetic obligation. I REFUTE NOTHING in g_cap-clamp.json: I re-ran all eight findings' repros on the current tree and every one reproduces. I do add one correction the checker's own repro carried: their `git show HEAD~1:src/capacity/levers.py | grep 'THAT FIFTH ONE IS CORRECTED TOO' -> 185:` prints 201: today, because HEAD moved between their run and mine -- the substance is unchanged.

findings.detail: REPRODUCED FIRST, THEN FIXED AS A DISTINCTION. The unreachable arm opened `no lift can be earned at all on this configuration, so no lift can be held at a ceiling either: {dead_reason}` and new_valve passed cap.valve's OWN `dead` prose as dead_reason -- two clauses of which assert the opposite. Now: `dead_reason` is replaced by `dead_facts`, a tuple of (arm, kind, numbers) records built in the SAME branches that build `dead`, over the closed set capacity/api.py::_CLAMP_BLOCKED_KINDS; capacity/api.py::_clamp_blocked_clause renders one sentence per arm in the clamp's own words; and the headline is about the clamp's event, not about earning. WHAT EACH KIND SAYS AND WHY IT IS TRUE, each checked against the arithmetic on every cell it appeared on: unarmed (11,253 expert + 12,160 vocabulary) 'NOT ARMED, so NO LIFT IS EVER EARNED on it: CAP_TARGETS=<t> does not arm this arm'; nonpositive (1,023 + 1,520) cap <= 0; never_pins (1,364, expert only) cap > the cull settling point; at_ceiling (7,843 + 4,560) 'EARNED AND REFUSED, WHICH IS NOT CLAMPED ... observe refuses by name as at_hard_ceiling BEFORE any lift is computed'; refused_unmasked (3,040) 'EARNED AND REFUSED ... LM_MASK_DEAD_ROWS=False makes observe refuse every one of them by name as dead_rows_unmasked'; inert (125 + 328) 'EARNED AND APPLIED AND MOVES NOTHING ... derive.lift_to(12, CAP_LIFT=0.08, CAP_LIFT_MIN=0) = 12 returns it unchanged'. BOTH ARMS ARE EXPLAINED ON EVERY UNREACHABLE CELL -- the unarmed records are in dead_facts and NOT in `dead`, which is the one structural difference between the two lists, because an unarmed arm is a perfectly good reason no lift of its can ever be clamped and cap.valve's prose never speaks of it. I ALSO CLOSED THE SECOND HALF OF THE REFUTATION (the two report lines that would disagree once observe exists): _clamp_gate now takes the UNREACHABLE arm only when `lifts` and `clamped` are both 0, and when CAP.counters rebuilds it with a non-zero ledger against a dead startup analysis the reachable arm prints and appends 'THE STARTUP ANALYSIS SAID NO LIFT COULD BE HELD AT A CEILING HERE AND THE LEDGER DISAGREES, so this line reports the LEDGER and not the analysis'. An unknown kind raises ValueError rather than rendering a blank clause.

AFTER: 0 of 25,344, and 0 printed occurrences of the string 'no lift can be earned at all' anywhere in the sweep. Named cells, run and pasted: {"CAP_TARGETS":"vocab","CAP_VOCAB_START":"1000"} -> 'Gate cap.clamp: UNREACHABLE (0 clamped of 0 lift(s) taken vs 0 clamped -- every earned lift applied in full) -- NO LIFT CAN BE HELD AT A HARD CEILING on this configuration, which is the only event this gate counts. A clamp needs three things IN ORDER ... : (expert) NOT ARMED, so NO LIFT IS EVER EARNED on it: CAP_TARGETS=vocab does not arm this arm ...; (vocabulary) EARNED AND REFUSED, WHICH IS NOT CLAMPED: the cap of 1000 is below its hard ceiling of 4096, so lifts ARE earned here, and LM_MASK_DEAD_ROWS=False makes observe refuse every one of them by name as dead_rows_unmasked ...'. {"CAP_TARGETS":"experts","CAP_FAB_START":"12","CAP_LIFT_MIN":"0"} -> '... The other four grounds run and pasted in my transcript: CAP_TARGETS=off (both unarmed), CAP_FAB_START=-5/CAP_VOCAB_START=-5 (both nonpositive), CAP_FAB_START=5000+CAP_VOCAB_START=4096 (both at_ceiling), CAP_FAB_START=3000/FAB_SLOTS=4096 (never_pins, 'sits above the cull's settling point of 1844'). Direct unit checks of all four gate states plus the ledger-disagreement clause: _clamp_gate('X',0,0,dead_facts=df) -> UNREACHABLE; (7,0) -> 'armed, did not fire ... 7 earned lift(s) and every one was applied IN FULL ... THE STARTUP ANALYSIS SAID NO LIFT COULD BE HELD AT A CEILING HERE AND THE LEDGER DISAGREES'; (7,2) -> FIRED; (7,2) with no dead_facts -> FIRED with no such clause; _clamp_blocked_clause('expert','bogus',{}) -> ValueError "cap.clamp: unknown blocked-kind 'bogus'; the closed set is ('unarmed', 'nonpositive', 'never_pins', 'at_ceiling', 'refused_unmasked', 'inert')".
